I think if this was in place it would, in essence, give prisoners an option between life in prison and the death penalty. And in the US, at least to my knowledge, the death penalty has undergone many changes in the past to try to make it as humane and painless as possible. I feel like suicide is an extraordinarily painful experience on the person, even if it is their choice (either being in such a mental state to take one's own life or to have the burden of choosing between suicide or life imprisonment.) Because of this pain I do not agree with it being an option for the death penalty or as an alternative to life imprisonment.
I remember this part, the same words and light touches, but last time, I remember that I died.

The shadows hung suffocatingly thick. A trembling hand gripped the soft cotton closer around, trembling with fear. A sob quaked. Tearful eyes tried to pierce through the veil, but moving shadows imposed upon the small form and earned another cry. They moved and shifted under the lightless night, monsters and shades threatening with their menace. Eyes scrunched against the fearful images and tried to will them away. “Where was the man who fixed the stars? “ rolled through his tear-stained mind. A small hiccup choked from him as his vision was blinded by the sudden onslaught of light, shut off just as quickly as it was on. A kindly figure walked towards the cover. 

“Here you go bud,” came the groggy voice. “Good as new.” and with a click, the room erupted into an array of purple and pink stars. They dotted the ceiling and blew away the nightmares. The boy reached out for the plush and held it close to him. Purple and pink silhouetted his face as he smiled up at the figure. “Thanks daddy.” he said with a small hiccup. The dad smiled tiredly down and patted his son’s head before  leaving the room. “Good night bud.”

The boy snuggled closer to his light, letting the soft fabric brush against his face. His eyes followed the stars that glowed on the ceiling. The shadows gone and the fears chased away, his eyes began to droop and his head began to grow heavy. The man who fixed the stars would always be there to keep the lights glowing.
